scenes.label: Same balance, different story
scenes.title: Same balance. Different story.
scenes.voiceover: Same balance. Same story? One customer's balance is steady. The other's has just fallen. A snapshot hides the difference. We designed features to reveal the context behind the number.

scenes.label: Features and hypotheses
scenes.title: Nine ways to reveal the context
scenes.voiceover: Lags preserve last month's values, adding recent context. Monthly changes expose sudden movement. Three-month averages estimate a customer's normal behavior. Relative balance and payroll compare today's values with that personal baseline, making changes comparable across customers. Card utilization relates balances to available credit, suggesting financial pressure. Six-month relative funds use a longer personal baseline. Relative usage measures debit and card activity against the customer's usual level, looking for disengagement. Monetary ranks represent a customer's position within the same month, putting amounts on comparable scales. Finally, exponential averages emphasize recent past behavior, so emerging changes matter more.

scenes.label: A fair comparison
scenes.title: Give every addition a fair test
scenes.voiceover: We compared each feature package with its reference model, retraining with five matched random seeds. We tracked ranking quality and profit, comparing results within each measurement.

scenes.label: All results together
scenes.title: Which signals helped?
scenes.voiceover: Here are the results together. Relative balance and payroll gave the largest ranking gain and were the only package to pass our screening rule. Monthly changes and averages had smaller positive gains. Lags and utilization did not improve this screen. For profit, longer funds history and relative usage improved both historical months. Exponential averaging was mixed. The columns measure different outcomes, so compare within each column.

scenes.label: Takeaway
scenes.title: The clearest signal was personal context
scenes.voiceover: Relative balance and payroll were our strongest ranking addition. Longer funds history and usage are promising profit candidates. These are historical findings; individual public gains remain unproven.
